clue.text: Hero potentially good to czar catching virus

indicators.note: catching means the rearranged letters hold the virus inside them
potentially says these letters could become something else, so they are rearranged

parts.note: HIV is the virus that causes AIDS

explanation.surface: Someone might become a hero by being good to the czar, even while carrying a virus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potentially' is the anagram signal and 'catching' the insertion. Yuri Zhivago is the hero of Pasternak's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Yuri Zhivago is the title character and protagonist of Pasternak's novel, so he is its hero.

clue.text: Pen sad epic novel about 1A's 26, leading character suffering this fate?

definitions.text: Pen sad epic novel about 1A's 26, leading character suffering this fate?

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the next piece
novel means new or fresh, so these letters are put into a new order
the first letter of the name suffers the fate in question, vanishing from it

parts.note: 1-across is Doctor Zhivago and 26 is kindred spirit: Zhivago's true love is Lara

explanation.surface: An invitation to write a sad, epic novel about Zhivago's beloved, whose main character meets a grim end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' is the anagram signal and 'about' the wrap. The leading character's letter disappears, and Lara herself vanishes at the end of Pasternak's book.
explanation.definitionFit: Lara vanishes from Zhivago's life and is said to have died in a camp, a vanishing that is exactly the fate described.

clue.text: Coach shortened odds saddling thoroughbred

indicators.note: saddling means the shortened word sits around the horse like a saddle on its back
shortened means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: the odds of something happening are its chance
an Arab is a thoroughbred breed of horse

explanation.surface: A racing tip: the odds shortened once a thoroughbred was saddled, with 'Coach' as the horse's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortened' drops the last letter, giving CHANC, and 'saddling' sits it around the horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A charabanc is an old-fashioned open motor coach used for outings.

clue.text: Say working men must lead state

indicators.note: must lead says the men come first, ahead of the other pieces

parts.note: OR, other ranks, are the ordinary soldiers, the men of the army
EG, for example, is what 'say' means when giving an instance
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A statement that, while the job is going on, the men have to be in charge of the state.
explanation.walkthrough: OR (other ranks) is the crossword's usual 'men'.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregon is one of the fifty states of the USA, on the Pacific coast.

clue.text: Nothing happening? Close

parts.note: zip is slang for nothing, as in 'zip, zero, nada'
what's up? asks what is happening, so up means going on

explanation.surface: Someone asks if nothing is going on, and is told the shop is closed.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark ends a separate sentence; 'Close' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To zip up a coat or bag is to fasten it shut, so it is a verb for closing.

clue.text: Play's opening leaves playwright bound to meddle

indicators.note: leaves means the picked letter departs from the playwright's name

parts.note: Harold Pinter was an English playwright

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to bound along is to lope, moving with long strides

explanation.surface: As a play opens, the playwright leaves, bound to interfere with it.
explanation.walkthrough: P, the 'opening' of Play's, 'leaves' PINTER to give INTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To interlope is to intrude into others' affairs without being wanted, which is meddling.

clue.text: See about skinning cats; approach gradually

indicators.note: skinning a word strips off its outside letters, leaving the inner ones

parts.note: to tend to something is to lean slowly in its direction

explanation.surface: Instructions concerning skinning cats, by easing into it slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: Skinning CATS removes C and S, leaving AT.
explanation.definitionFit: To see about a problem is to deal with or look after it, which is what attending to it means.

clue.text: That hurt, Glaswegian hooligan admitted

parts.note: ow is what someone cries when something has hurt them
ned is Scottish slang, especially in Glasgow, for a young hoodlum

explanation.surface: A victim saying it hurt, and that a hooligan from Glasgow confessed.
explanation.walkthrough: NED is Scottish slang for a young troublemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: To own, or own up to, something is to confess it, so owned means admitted.

clue.text: Rich ruler caught and hung in reorganisation

indicators.note: caught means heard, so the ruler's title is taken as spoken

parts.note: a sheik is an Arab ruler, often thought of as fabulously wealthy
a picture that is hung is up on the wall

explanation.surface: A wealthy ruler is captured and executed during a political shake-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' is the sound indicator: SHEIK said aloud with one common pronunciation gives SHAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: A shake-up is a radical restructuring of an organisation, which is a reorganisation.

clue.text: Idiot and ice largely doing for this

definitions.text: Idiot and ice largely doing for this

parts.note: tit is British slang for a fool

indicators.note: largely means most of each word, so each loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Blaming the sinking of the famous liner on a fool at the helm and, chiefly, an iceberg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' trims AND to AN and ICE to IC. The whole clue is the definition: a careless captain and an iceberg did for the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titanic was the liner sunk by an iceberg in 1912, so ice did for it.

clue.text: Stoppage of tram maybe ill-starred, involving 1Ac

parts.note: a tram is one kind of car, as in a tramcar

indicators.note: involving means the rearranged letters wrap around the next piece
ill means badly, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the figure 1 gives the Roman numeral I, and Ac is written as it stands

explanation.surface: A cross-reference makes this look like a note about a tram stopping in the 1-across story.
explanation.walkthrough: '1Ac' poses as a cross-reference to 1-across but is read literally: the figure as a Roman numeral, then Ac. 'ill' is the anagram signal, giving D...ARREST, and 'involving' wraps it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardiac arrest is the sudden stopping of the heart.

clue.text: Bad atmosphere when publisher punches fellow publisher?

indicators.note: punches means the pieces go through into the middle of the fellow

parts.note: a peer is a fellow, an equal; here an equal of the other publisher
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
OUP is Oxford University Press, a publisher

explanation.surface: Things turn nasty when one publisher thumps a rival publisher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punches' puts AS + OUP into PEER, the publisher's equal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pea-souper is a thick yellow London smog, an unpleasantly dense atmosphere.

clue.text: Purge one recalled as the worst time

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: to purge something is to rid yourself of it
an means one, as in 'an apple'

explanation.surface: A purge, looked back on, was the worst period of all.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point of something, its absolute worst moment.

clue.text: In reverse of normality, a bear market with ever-rising prices

indicators.note: reverse says the letters found are read backwards
In says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Financial jargon: when normality goes into reverse, a bear market sees prices rising.
explanation.walkthrough: A bear market normally has falling prices, so a market whose prices only climb sounds like a reversal of it.
explanation.definitionFit: On an auction site bids only ever go up until the sale closes, so prices keep climbing.

clue.text: Half four at lido, train regularly with greater confidence

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of these words, here the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: An instruction to go and train at the lido at half past four, sticking to a regular schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half four' looks like a fraction to work out, but it is just British for 4:30. A lido is an outdoor public swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortiori is Latin for 'from the stronger', used when a conclusion follows even more surely.

clue.text: Mime artist clutches belly, absorbing one in character

indicators.note: in means the whole assembly goes inside the character

parts.note: an air is a manner or character, as in 'an air of mystery'

indicators.note: clutches means the artist holds the next piece inside

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: absorbing means the belly takes the numeral into itself

parts.note: gut is another word for belly
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A mime artist clasping their stomach, taking on a role while staying in character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mime artist' looks like one phrase, but only 'Mime' is the definition. 'absorbing', 'clutches' and 'in' are three nested insertions.
explanation.definitionFit: Air guitar is miming playing a guitar along to music, with no instrument.

clue.text: Too ambitious removing clothing, lovers agree, shivering

indicators.note: removing clothing strips the outer letters from the word, as if undressing it
shivering means shaking, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Two lovers undress, agree they are cold, and shiver.
explanation.walkthrough: Stripping LOVERS gives OVER; 'shivering' shakes AGREE into EAGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone overeager is too keen to succeed, which is being excessively ambitious.

clue.text: Peg on a boat, Dicky to help at home

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for weak or unreliable, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: someone who is at home is in

explanation.surface: Someone called Dicky is pegged to help out at home on a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a name but is the anagram indicator, British slang for shaky (a dicky heart).
explanation.definitionFit: A thole pin is a wooden peg set in a boat's gunwale to hold an oar in place while rowing.

clue.text: People reportedly unable to speak freely, Nijinsky among others

parts.note: a race is a people, a group sharing descent

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: someone hoarse has a rough voice and cannot speak easily

explanation.surface: People said to be unable to speak freely, among them the dancer Nijinsky.
explanation.walkthrough: Nijinsky suggests the ballet dancer, but it is the 1970 Triple Crown winner, named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: Nijinsky was a famous racehorse who won the English Triple Crown in 1970, so he is an example.

clue.text: Elite in revolution deprived of a valuable estate?

indicators.note: in revolution means turned round, so the letters are read backwards
deprived of means the letter is taken away from the word

parts.note: the cream of society is its elite

explanation.surface: The elite, overthrown in a revolution, lose a valuable estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'estate' suggests land but means an estate car, the British name for a station wagon; a Merc (Mercedes) can be one. 'deprived of' takes A from CREAM to leave CREM.
explanation.definitionFit: A Merc is a Mercedes, an expensive car made in estate versions as well as saloons.

clue.text: Arranged upper limits on losing love?

definitions.text: Arranged upper limits on losing love?

indicators.note: limits means the rearranged letters hem in the next piece
arranged means put in order, so these letters are reordered
losing means the letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: An agreed cap on what each partner loses when love ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arranged' is the anagram signal, giving PRE...UP; 'losing' drops love's O, and 'limits' encloses what is left. Read whole, the clue describes the contract.
explanation.definitionFit: A prenuptial agreement settles beforehand how property is shared if the marriage fails.

clue.text: Millionaire leaving his estate for good, born during Christmas

definitions.text: Millionaire leaving his estate for good

indicators.note: during means the letter is placed inside Christmas

parts.note: Noel is another name for Christmas

explanation.surface: A rich man born at Christmas leaves his wealth to charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Nobel left most of his fortune to found the prizes named after him, a bequest for the good of humanity.

clue.text: Gloomy book to exfiltrate for publication

parts.note: to leak documents is to sneak them out so they can be published

explanation.surface: A dark book has been smuggled out of the country so it can be published.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleak describes a dismal, cheerless outlook or place, which is gloomy.

clue.text: Lingerie on bed in Durham?

definitions.meaning: the River Wear flows through Durham, so on its bed you are under the Wear

explanation.surface: Lingerie on a bed somewhere in Durham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' suggests a bedroom; it is a riverbed. Durham is a city in north-east England on the River Wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingerie is women's underclothing, a fancier word for underwear.

clue.text: Russian agreed communist rose to the challenge

parts.note: da is Russian for yes, an agreement
red is a common name for a communist

explanation.surface: A Russian communist agreed and rose to meet the challenge.
explanation.definitionFit: To dare is to have the courage to take something on, meeting a challenge head-on.

clue.text: Marking certainly stops poet working

indicators.note: stops means the word plugs the gap inside, like a stopper
working means being worked into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: yes, certainly

explanation.surface: Grading papers certainly stops a poet getting on with his work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges POET into E...POT, and 'stops' plugs YES into it.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyespot is an eye-like spot of colour, like those on a peacock's tail or a butterfly's wing.

clue.text: Refuse roubles Onegin brought to the west

parts.note: R is an abbreviation for rouble, Russia's currency

indicators.note: brought to the west means reading leftward, so the name runs backwards in an across answer

parts.note: Eugene Onegin is Pushkin's verse-novel hero

explanation.surface: Onegin brings his roubles to the West and then refuses something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Onegin' gives his first name, EUGENE, which reads ENEGUE backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To renegue (more often renege) is to go back on a promise or decline to honour it.

clue.text: Nice bloody vodka for one true love

parts.note: nice means kind
blood is red, so bloody suggests red
vodka is an example of a spirit

explanation.surface: Someone nice who drinks Bloody Mary vodka cocktails turns out to be one's true love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' could be the French city, but it simply means KIND.
explanation.definitionFit: A kindred spirit is someone whose outlook matches yours, a soulmate.
